newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Banca Agricola 96 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Romania Banca Agricola 96 profit up.

text.p: Romania's state-run bank Banca Agricola SA (BA) said on Thursday its net profit almost doubled last year to 147 billion lei from 73.6 billion in 1995.
The increase reflected better management of the bank's expenditure, which pushed gross profit to 165.5 billion lei from 142 billion at end-1995, a bank report said.

Romania's State Ownership Fund holds around 54 percent of the bank's end-1996 share capital of 30.7 billion lei and regional ownership funds 29.9 percent. The rest is held by local companies and individuals.

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development last year allowed its equity conversion rights on a $12 million technology loan to BA to lapse due to delays in a bank selloff law, a key demand under accords with international lenders.

Earlier this week, the centrist coalition government approved a bank privatisation bill which failed twice to pass parliament under the former leftist administration. The bill is to be discussed by parliament next week.
Bank privatisation is a benchmark for restoring loans from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, which are expected to discuss new credits for Romania later this month.
Banca Agricola specialises in financing agriculture and has been the main channel for government aid to farmers.
The bank's report said its own restructuring became an issue during negotiations earlier this year on securing a World Bank Financial and Enterprise Structural Adjustment Loan.
Restructuring plans envisage the split of commercial activities from those as a state agent as well as a clarification of its soft loan portfolio, it said.
Around 87 percent of BA revenues came from its lending rates, which averaged about 36 percent in 1996, when total assets were 8.2 trillion lei, or 41.5 percent up from 1995.
Half the bank's 1996 net profit went to its development fund. It is to pay a 40 percent dividend, the same as in 1995.
